problem_statement: The network stack should support a Kconfig option to enable or disable checksum offloading at compile time. When checksum offloading is enabled and the underlying ethernet driver advertises hardware checksum capabilities via get_capabilities(), the stack must skip calculating TX and RX checksums (leaving them zero, for the hardware to fill). When offloading is disabled or the driver does not advertise the capability, the stack must calculate checksums in software. The test uses two virtual ethernet interfaces — one advertising offload capabilities and one not — to verify that packets on the offloading-enabled interface have zero checksums while those on the disabled interface have non-zero checksums, for both UDP and ICMP, fragmented and non-fragmented, IPv4 and IPv6.
twister_command: scripts/twister -p native_sim/native/64 -T tests/net/checksum_offload -s tests/net/checksum_offload/net.offload -s net.offload -O twister-out --no-clean -W

verification.reason: The test Kconfig requires the exact symbol name NET_CHECKSUM_OFFLOAD_SUPPORTED to exist, but the statement never names it. The two-option structure (SUPPORTED + OFFLOAD) is also not described, making the required interface unguessable. This is fixable by adding the Kconfig names and their relationship to the statement.

problems.detail: The hidden test Kconfig explicitly references CONFIG_NET_CHECKSUM_OFFLOAD_SUPPORTED (setting it to default y), but the problem statement only vaguely says 'a Kconfig option to enable or disable checksum offloading' without naming either the driver-selecting option (NET_CHECKSUM_OFFLOAD_SUPPORTED) or the user-facing option (NET_CHECKSUM_OFFLOAD). A developer cannot reliably guess the exact name 'NET_CHECKSUM_OFFLOAD_SUPPORTED' and the two-option structure (promptless SUPPORTED selected by drivers, plus user-facing OFFLOAD that depends on it and defaults to y).

leak_check.leak_detail: The final sentence explicitly mentions the hidden test setup and expected results ('The test uses...'). It does not reveal the implementation approach (the Kconfig design or net_if behavior), but it is a mention of the tests and should be reworded as a behavioral requirement.
leak_check.suggested_statement: The network stack should support Kconfig options to enable or disable checksum offloading at compile time. The option CONFIG_NET_CHECKSUM_OFFLOAD_SUPPORTED is a promptless option that must be selected by ethernet drivers that support hardware checksum offloading. The user-facing option CONFIG_NET_CHECKSUM_OFFLOAD depends on CONFIG_NET_CHECKSUM_OFFLOAD_SUPPORTED and defaults to y; it enables or disables checksum offloading. When checksum offloading is enabled and the underlying ethernet driver advertises hardware checksum capabilities via get_capabilities(), the stack must skip calculating TX and RX checksums (leaving them zero, for the hardware to fill). When offloading is disabled or the driver does not advertise the capability, the stack must calculate checksums in software. The behavior must apply to UDP and ICMP, fragmented and non-fragmented packets, and IPv4 and IPv6.
